mem.t: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.

lessons.title: Chewing the Cud
lessons.theme: Meditation means chewing God’s word over and over until it becomes life

v: How I love your law! It is my meditation all day.
But Mary kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.

lessons.still: Choose one short verse, such as “Yahweh is my shepherd.” Don’t hurry on to the next line. Simply say it slowly three times, stressing a different word each time. Like a sweet held on the tongue, let its flavor slowly melt into your heart.
teach: Cattle have a peculiar habit: they swallow their grass first, then, while resting, bring it back up to chew it slowly—and only then is it truly digested. Many of us read the Bible the way we eat fast food: one gulp and we’re gone. Meditation is like chewing the cud—bringing back the word we have taken in and chewing it again and again until it becomes nourishment.

In Joshua, the Hebrew word for “meditate” carries the sense of murmuring under one’s breath, quietly repeating to oneself. The psalmist says God’s law is his “meditation all day.” Mary did the same: she did not fully understand what was happening, yet she “kept all these sayings, pondering them in her heart.” Meditation is not emptying the mind but filling the heart with God’s word; it is not chasing unusual experiences but letting truth slowly unfold within us.

Reading Scripture puts food in the mouth; meditation chews it; obedience digests it into life. We often think our spiritual problem is that we haven’t read enough, but more often it is that we haven’t chewed long enough. Better to take one verse all the way in than to skim ten chapters.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Live from the heart by the Spirit, not from the head by yourself. Meditation is not analyzing with the brain and piling up knowledge; it is receiving with the heart through the Holy Spirit. Read with the head, and Scripture easily becomes exam material; read with the heart, and it becomes food. Among the eight steps of changing our mindset, “Information” must pass through meditation before it can become “Revelation.”
q: Who is God? — What patience does God show you in being willing to feed you with his word?
Who am I? — Is your Bible reading more like grabbing fast food or like chewing slowly?
How shall I respond? — Which verse will you “chew the cud” on today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, he answered three times, “It is written” (Matthew 4). After forty days of fasting, God’s word came out of his mouth without his needing to open a book—the fruit of years of pondering it in his heart. He said, “Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God’s mouth.”
lessons.pray: Lord, I often rush through your word without letting it into my heart. Teach me, like Mary, to keep your words and ponder them in my heart. Holy Spirit, open my heart so that your word becomes my food and turns into life within me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Choose just one verse today and meditate on it morning, noon and evening
Circle one word in the verse and ask, “What is this word saying to me?”
Before bed, write one sentence: the flavor this verse released in my heart today
lessons.noon: “How I love your law! It is my meditation all day.” — Lord, right now I chew on your word once more.

lessons.title: A Tree by the Streams
lessons.theme: Blessed is the one who meditates on God’s word day and night

v: Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
but his delight is in the LORD’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.
He will be like a tree planted by the streams of water, that produces its fruit in its season, whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall prosper.

lessons.still: Picture yourself as a tree, your roots reaching downward in search of water. Quietly ask the Lord, “Where are my roots going down right now?” Then say, “Lord, I want to sink my roots into your word.”
teach: In dry country, the grass by the roadside turns brown after a few days of sun, but the tree beside the stream stays green all year round. The difference is not who tries harder but whose roots have reached the water. Meditating on God’s word means sending the roots of our life down into living water.

Psalm 1 uses three verbs to trace the gradual slide into sin: to “walk” in the counsel of the wicked, to “stand” on the path of sinners, to “sit” in the seat of scoffers—from listening, to lingering, to settling down. The blessed person turns the other way: his “delight” is in Yahweh’s law, and he “meditates day and night.” The result: fruit in its season and leaves that do not wither. Notice the word “planted”—the tree did not walk to the stream by itself; it was planted there.

Blessing does not begin with outward success but with inward “delight.” If meditation is only a duty, it soon dries up; when it becomes a delight, it becomes a day-and-night habit. Let us ask God to change our appetite, so that we love his word more than the endless stream of information on our phones.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life first, then relationships, then ministry. The tree by the stream has roots first, then fruit; first a life of meditation, then a life that bears fruit. The human view looks at outward prosperity; God’s view looks at the hidden source within. Our perspective shifts from earthly things to heavenly things.
q: Who is God? — God “planted” you by the streams. What does that say about who is the source of your growth?
Who am I? — Lately, what kinds of voices have you been walking with, standing among, and sitting under?
How shall I respond? — Which stretch of time you would normally spend scrolling your phone will you use for meditation today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink!” (John 7:37). He himself is the source of living water. He also often withdrew to the wilderness to pray (Luke 5:16), drawing strength from the Father. So all his life his leaf never withered, and in due season he bore the fruit of obedience.
lessons.pray: Lord, I want to be that blessed person. Change my appetite so that I delight in your word and meditate on it day and night. Plant me by your streams of water; let my roots go deep, let me bear fruit in season, and let my leaf not wither even in days of drought. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the three voices you spent the most time listening to today
Replace one stretch of phone-scrolling with five minutes meditating on Psalm 1
Draw a tree, and among its roots write a verse you will meditate on
lessons.noon: “But his delight is in the LORD’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.” — Lord, right now I sink my roots into your word.

lessons.title: Hiding the Word in My Heart
lessons.theme: Memorizing Scripture means carrying God’s word with you wherever you go

v: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.
With my whole heart I have sought you. Don’t let me wander from your commandments.
I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.
Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.

lessons.still: Close your eyes and try to recite this week’s verse, Joshua 1:8, without looking. If you can’t remember part of it, that’s fine—open your Bible, look again, then close your eyes and try once more. Treat this as a walk with the Lord, not an exam.
teach: Money in the bank and cash in your pocket serve different purposes: in an emergency, what you can pull out right away is the money you carry. Scripture is the same. Verses we have read are like savings stored on a bookshelf; verses we have memorized travel with us, ready to be drawn out in the moment of temptation, fear, or when someone needs comfort.

The psalmist asks, “How can a young man keep his way pure?” The answer is “by living according to your word,” and the method is “I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.” To “hide” here means to treasure something precious. Paul also urges us to let the word of Christ “dwell in you richly,” and then to teach and admonish one another. Memorizing is not only for ourselves; it is also for building others up.

Memorization is not a memory contest; it is letting God’s word become the “mother tongue” of the heart. The method is simple: one verse a week, written on a card, recited together with its reference, three times morning and evening. Don’t worry about going slowly—one verse a week means fifty-two verses living in your heart by the end of the year.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Scripture is my standard. A standard that stays only in a book is of no use in a crisis; hidden in the heart, it becomes guidance available at any moment. Memorization is also a practice of humility—admitting that my own thoughts are unreliable and being willing to let God’s words replace mine and reign in my heart.
q: Who is God? — God is willing to entrust his words to you as a treasure. What kind of grace is this?
Who am I? — How many verses are you “carrying with you” in your heart right now?
How shall I respond? — What method will you use this week to memorize Joshua 1:8?
lessons.jesus: At twelve years old, Jesus sat in the temple asking and answering the teachers, and all who heard him were amazed at his understanding (Luke 2:47). Later—in the wilderness, in his preaching, on the cross—Old Testament words were constantly on his lips; even his dying cries came from the Psalms (Psalm 22:1; 31:5). God’s word had long been hidden in his heart.
lessons.pray: Lord, I want to hide your word in my heart so that I might not sin against you. Help me keep up the discipline of memorization—not to impress anyone, but to know you better and obey you more fully. Let the word of Christ dwell in me richly and flow from my lips to bless others. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write Joshua 1:8 on a card and recite it three times morning and evening
Divide this week’s verse into three parts and memorize one more part each day
Share a verse you know by heart with someone who needs it today
lessons.noon: “I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.” — Lord, right now I treasure your word in my heart.

lessons.title: Carrying Scripture Through the Day
lessons.theme: Sitting, walking, lying down and rising up—walking with God’s word

v: These words, which I command you today, shall be on your heart;
and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.
when I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches.

lessons.still: Think ahead to four moments in your day: getting up, going out, eating, and lying down. Quietly pair a short verse with each moment, like setting out four lamps in advance along the path of your day.
teach: People used to tie a knot in a handkerchief to remind themselves not to forget something. God likewise taught Israel to “tie” his words into daily life in all kinds of ways: keeping them on their hearts, teaching them to their children, talking of them whether sitting or walking. Meditation is not just a slot of time in the morning; it is a melody playing in the background of the whole day.

Deuteronomy 6 names four everyday settings: “when you sit in your house,” “when you walk by the way,” “when you lie down,” and “when you rise up”—covering home, going out, rest and new beginnings. God’s word is not meant to be kept in a religious compartment but to seep into every crack of ordinary life. David too says that he remembers God on his bed and thinks about him in the night watches; even sleepless hours became times of meditation.

Here is a practical approach: in the morning, choose one verse; at midday, pray a one-line arrow prayer; in the evening, recall where that verse met you during the day. Little by little, Scripture will surface on its own while you wait at a red light, stand in a queue, or are misunderstood—that is the Holy Spirit reminding you.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Holy Spirit is my guide. Carrying Scripture through the day gives the Spirit “material” to remind us with. Earthly, temporary things often fill our thoughts; Scripture lifts our eyes back to heavenly, eternal things. The focus is on Jesus, not on our circumstances.
q: Who is God? — God wants to be part of your sitting, walking, lying down and rising up. What kind of God is he?
Who am I? — At what time of your day are you most likely to forget God?
How shall I respond? — In which everyday moment today will you set down a verse of Scripture?
lessons.jesus: Jesus often drew his teaching from everyday life: a sower, the birds of the air, the lilies of the field, yeast, a woman searching for a lost coin. In his eyes, ordinary life was the very place to walk with the Father. He taught on the road, at the dinner table, in a boat—God’s word and his life were never separated.
lessons.pray: Lord, I don’t want to remember you only in the morning and then forget you all day. Let your word go with me as I sit, walk, lie down and rise up. When I am busy and scattered, let the Holy Spirit remind me of a verse; when I wake in the night, let me think of you. May my day be filled with your word. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Make this week’s verse your phone’s lock screen
Before each meal, meditate on this week’s verse once before you start eating
Before bed, recall: at what moment today did this verse come to mind?
lessons.noon: “I remember you on my bed, and think about you in the night watches.” — Lord, right now I remember you in the midst of ordinary life.

lessons.title: Meditation Leads to Obedience
lessons.theme: True meditation ends with turning our steps toward God

v: I considered my ways, and turned my steps to your statutes.
I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments.
One who has my commandments and keeps them, that person is one who loves me. One who loves me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him, and will reveal myself to him.”

lessons.still: Recall one verse you meditated on this week and quietly ask, “Lord, what specific action does this verse want me to change?” Wait for a while, then write down whatever comes to your heart.
teach: You can know a recipe by heart, but if you never cook, your family still goes hungry. Meditation that stops at admiration and being moved is like endlessly reading recipes. The order in Joshua 1:8 is clear: meditate day and night “that you may observe to do” it. The end point of meditation is not feeling moved but taking action.

The psalmist says, “I considered my ways, and turned my steps to your statutes.” After considering comes “turning my steps,” and then “I will hurry, and not delay, to obey.” Meditation is like a mirror that shows the gap between my ways and God’s statutes; once I see it, I adjust my steps at once. Jesus also said that the one who has his commandments and keeps them is the one who loves him—and he will reveal himself to that person. Obedience opens the door to knowing the Lord more deeply.

This week we have learned: meditation is chewing the cud → a tree by the streams → hiding the word in our hearts → carrying Scripture through the day → and today, meditation leads to obedience. In the eight steps of changing our mindset, meditation is the bridge from “Revelation” to “Conviction” and “Practice.” Next week we will let this obedience grow into worship and thanksgiving.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Change your mindset and you change your life; change your life and you change your lifestyle. Meditation changes the mindset; obedience changes the life and the lifestyle. Meditation without obedience actually makes us proud—we know more yet still rule ourselves. Only obedient meditation lets Jesus reign.
q: Who is God? — Why does God link “revealing himself” with “keeping his commandments”?
Who am I? — Is there a verse you have read many times but never put into practice?
How shall I respond? — What will you “turn your steps” to do right away today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me, and to accomplish his work” (John 4:34). For him, God’s word was not only pondered but eaten and lived out. He went from meditation to obedience, all the way to the cross, “becoming obedient to death.”
lessons.pray: Lord, I don’t want to be only a hearer of the word but a doer as well. Let your word light up my path, so that when I see, I turn my steps toward you and hurry to obey without delay. I want to show my love for you by obeying; please reveal yourself to me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: From the verses you meditated on this week, choose one specific action and complete it today
Note one act of obedience you have kept putting off, and take the first step today
Recite Joshua 1:8 to a spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “I will hurry, and not delay, to obey your commandments.” — Lord, right now I turn my steps toward you.
